components.rationale: Language: the neg/->/forall/exists fragment, with bot, and, or reached by definition (sheet 10; P2 55-57; def:p02-hfa-setting 26-28). Schemas A1-A3, forall1, forall2, exists1 and rules MP, existential elimination and Gen with their side conditions are displayed on the sheet (11-19); the P2.2 definition adopts that sheet as H_FOL and restates the MP, Gen and existential-elimination clauses with their conditions (54-76). Equality convention stated: 'equality: none (no equality axiom schemas)' (sheet 10), 'equality-free' (P2 57), 'r=t is not an atom of this fragment' (HFA 28), equality excluded (P14 162). The rule display lives on the registry sheet as CONVENTIONS.md 'Calculus registry' requires for editorial rule displays.

Statement: thm:p02-hilbert-fol-deduction (85-97) over the dependency-annotated relation whose Gen and existential-elimination clauses carry the free-variable conditions (68-75), and says it does not license generalizing a variable free in a supporting premise; the stronger support form is thm:p02-w02-p02-025-discharge (body 122-141). Proof with written steps: the supplement annex 21-59 and the full case analysis at the w02-p02-025 annex 168-328 (premise = phi, other premise, axiom, MP, Gen with phi in/out of support, existential elimination with phi in/out of support, each with written lines and supports, plus the converse), resting on the written five-line identity derivation (annex 12-28), the written nineteen-line permutation derivation with every schema instance and MP antecedent checked (30-121), and the written concatenation/support-restriction lemma (123-166). The warning at body 186-199 shows why the restriction is needed. No citation or label stands in for a step.

Separate systems with separate assumptions: H_CPL is the neg/-> sheet with plain formula sequences and MP only (PROP 12-24; CPL sheet 7-11) and has its own deduction theorem thm:p02-hilbert-deduction (PROP 26-34); H_FOL is a different sheet with quantifier schemas, dependency-annotated lines and restricted Gen/existential elimination (P2 54-83), and its deduction theorem is a distinct result. P14 149-176 presents the two sheets separately and names the three first-order variable checks. Derived rules are kept apart: the FOL identity and permutation are given as their own empty-support derivations rather than imported from the propositional deduction theorem (K25 37-47, 83-88, 361-368); the only use of the propositional basis theorem is the declared A1-A3/MP lifting lemma, with exact supports and no Gen, existential elimination or equality (HFA 18-23, 40-56).

Composite: GOAL-01, GOAL-02 and GOAL-03 are each covered at their stated standing (display; statement with written proof; distinctness). The original row's hypotheses are kept: the FOL system is a Hilbert-style system with a deduction theorem carrying the generalization/free-variable restriction, built on the propositional Hilbert system of D-P2-001 (sheet:hilbert-cpl, thm:p02-hilbert-deduction) without being conflated with it; the equality-free scope is announced. No narrower unannounced domain, different named result, or unproved dependency presented as proved.
